summary: The article provides generally accurate information regarding investing in US stocks from India, including LRS limits and tax implications, but contains a likely wrong claim about the LTCG tax rate for US stocks.

claims.claim: Apple's capital expenditure stood at $10.959 billion in 2023.
claims.note: Apple's annual capital expenditures for 2023 was $10.959 billion.

claims.claim: Under LRS, Indian residents can remit up to USD 2,50,000 (approximately ₹2 crores, depending on exchange rates) per financial year (April 1 to March 31) for various purposes, including overseas investments in shares and mutual funds.
claims.note: The LRS allows resident individuals to remit up to USD 2,50,000 per financial year (April 1 to March 31) for permissible current or capital account transactions, including overseas investments.

claims.claim: If you sell US stocks within 24 months of purchase, any profit is considered a short-term capital gain. This gain is added to your total income and taxed according to your applicable income tax slab rates.
claims.note: Short-term capital gains (STCG) from US stocks (held for less than 24 months) are added to the investor's total income and taxed at their applicable income tax slab rate.

claims.claim: If you sell US stocks after holding them for more than 24 months, the profit is treated as a long-term capital gain. This is taxed at a rate of 12.5% without the benefit of indexation for sales on or after July 23, 2024.
claims.note: Long-term capital gains (LTCG) on US stocks (held for more than 24 months) are taxed at 12.5% without indexation benefits for sales on or after July 23, 2024.

claims.claim: Dividends received from US stocks are typically subject to a 25% withholding tax in the US. However, under the DTAA, you can claim a credit for this tax paid in the US when filing your income tax return in India.
claims.note: Dividends from US stocks are subject to a 25% withholding tax in the US under the India-US DTAA, and Indian investors can claim a credit for this tax when filing their Indian income tax return.

claims.claim: Generally, capital gains on the sale of US stocks are taxed only in India for Indian residents, as per the DTAA. You may need to provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) to the US tax authorities to avoid US capital gains tax.
claims.note: Under the India-US DTAA and US domestic law, capital gains on the sale of US stocks by Indian residents are generally taxed only in India, as the US does not tax non-resident aliens on such gains. A TRC is generally not needed to avoid US capital gains tax, as the US does not levy it on non-residents.

claims.claim: She will pay 20% tax on this gain in India, with the benefit of indexation.
claims.note: Long-term capital gains on US stocks are taxed at 12.5% without the benefit of indexation for sales on or after July 23, 2024. The article states 20% with indexation, which was the rate before Budget 2024.
